# Mapper

The `Strawchemy` mapper, whose decorators and field factories generate a schema from SQLAlchemy models.

## `Strawchemy` {#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy}

[source](https://github.com/gazorby/strawchemy/blob/v0.24.0/src/strawchemy/mapper.py#L74)

```python
Strawchemy(config: StrawchemyConfig | SupportedDialect, strawberry_config: StrawberryConfig | None = None) -> None
```

Main entry point for integrating SQLAlchemy models with Strawberry GraphQL.

This class provides a cohesive interface to generate Strawberry GraphQL types,
inputs, filters, and fields based on SQLAlchemy models. It manages configuration,
type registration, and various factories for DTO generation.

**Attributes:**

[`registry`](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-registry) | <code>StrawberryRegistry</code> | The registry for Strawberry types.
[`filter`](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-filter) |  | Factory for creating boolean filter input types.
[`aggregate_filter`](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-aggregate_filter) |  | Factory for creating aggregate filter input types.
[`distinct_on`](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-distinct_on) |  | Decorator for creating distinct_on enum types.

Initializes the Strawchemy instance.

Sets up the configuration, registry, and various DTO factories
required for type and field generation.

**Parameters:**

Name | Type | Description | Default
---- | ---- | ----------- | -------
`config` | <code>[StrawchemyConfig](/v0.24.0/reference/config#strawchemy-config-base-StrawchemyConfig) \| SupportedDialect</code> | A StrawchemyConfig instance or a supported dialect string     (e.g., "postgresql", "mysql") to initialize a default config. | *required*
`strawberry_config` | <code>StrawberryConfig \| None</code> | A StrawberryConfig instance to initialize the registry. If not provided, a default StrawberryConfig will be used. | <code>None</code>

### `create` {#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-create}

```python
create(input_type: type[Any], resolver: Any | None = None, *, validation: ValidationProtocol[T] | None = None, **field_kwargs: Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]) -> Any
```

Creates a Strawberry GraphQL mutation field for creating new model instances.

This method generates a mutation field that handles the creation of
SQLAlchemy model instances based on the provided input type. It integrates
with Strawchemy's strawberry system for data persistence and allows for
custom validation.

**Parameters:**

Name | Type | Description | Default
---- | ---- | ----------- | -------
`input_type` | <code>[type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[Any]</code> | The Strawberry input type representing the data for creating a new model instance. This should be a `MappedGraphQLDTO`. | *required*
`resolver` | <code>Any \| None</code> | An optional custom resolver function for the mutation. If not provided, Strawchemy will use a default resolver. | <code>None</code>
`validation` | <code>ValidationProtocol[T] \| None</code> | An optional validation protocol instance to validate the input data before creation. | <code>None</code>
`**field_kwargs` | <code>Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]</code> | Common ``strawberry.field`` / repository arguments (see ``MutationFieldKwargs``); ``graphql_type`` sets the mutation return type. | <code>{}</code>

**Returns:**

Type | Description
---- | -----------
<code>Any</code> | A `StrawchemyCreateMutationField` instance, which is a specialized
<code>Any</code> | StrawberryField configured for create mutations.

### `create_input` {#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-create_input}

```python

```

### `delete` {#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-delete}

```python
delete(filter_input: type[BooleanFilterDTO] | None = None, resolver: Any | None = None, **field_kwargs: Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]) -> Any
```

Creates a Strawberry GraphQL mutation field for deleting model instances.

This method generates a mutation field that handles the deletion of
SQLAlchemy model instances. Deletion can be based on filter criteria
provided via `filter_input` or by ID if the `filter_input` is structured
to accept primary key(s). It integrates with Strawchemy's strawberry
system for data persistence.

**Parameters:**

Name | Type | Description | Default
---- | ---- | ----------- | -------
`filter_input` | <code>[type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[BooleanFilterDTO] \| None</code> | The Strawberry input type used to filter which model instances should be deleted. This should be a `BooleanFilterDTO`. If deleting by ID, this DTO should contain the ID field(s). If None, the mutation might be configured to delete a single record based on an ID passed directly (implementation dependent). | <code>None</code>
`resolver` | <code>Any \| None</code> | An optional custom resolver function for the mutation. If not provided, Strawchemy will use a default resolver. | <code>None</code>
`**field_kwargs` | <code>Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]</code> | Common ``strawberry.field`` / repository arguments (see ``MutationFieldKwargs``); ``graphql_type`` sets the mutation return type. | <code>{}</code>

**Returns:**

Type | Description
---- | -----------
<code>Any</code> | A `StrawchemyDeleteMutationField` instance, which is a specialized
<code>Any</code> | StrawberryField configured for delete mutations.

### `field` {#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-field}

```python
field(resolver: Any | None = None, *, filter_input: type[BooleanFilterDTO] | bool | None = None, order_by_input: FieldSpec | type[OrderByDTO] | None = None, default_order_by: Sequence[OrderByExpr] | OrderByExpr | None = None, pagination: bool | DefaultOffsetPagination | None = None, distinct_on: FieldSpec | type[EnumDTO] | None = None, arguments: list[StrawberryArgument] | None = None, model_field: str | None = None, id_field_name: str | None = None, root_aggregations: bool = False, filter_statement: FilterStatementCallable | None = None, execution_options: dict[str, Any] | None = None, query_hook: QueryHookCallable[Any] | Sequence[QueryHookCallable[Any]] | None = None, repository_type: AnyRepositoryType | None = None, root_field: bool = True, **field_kwargs: Unpack[OutputFieldKwargs]) -> Any
```

Creates a Strawberry GraphQL field with enhanced SQLAlchemy capabilities.

This method extends the standard Strawberry field creation by integrating
SQLAlchemy-specific features like automatic filtering, ordering, pagination,
and aggregations based on SQLAlchemy models.

**Parameters:**

Name | Type | Description | Default
---- | ---- | ----------- | -------
`resolver` | <code>Any \| None</code> | The resolver function for the field. If not provided, Strawchemy will attempt to generate one based on the model. | <code>None</code>
`filter_input` | <code>[type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[BooleanFilterDTO] \| bool \| None</code> | The input type for filtering results. | <code>None</code>
`order_by_input` | <code>FieldSpec \| [type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[OrderByDTO] \| None</code> | The input type for ordering results. | <code>None</code>
`default_order_by` | <code>Sequence[OrderByExpr] \| OrderByExpr \| None</code> | Default ordering for a list field as one or more SQLAlchemy column ordering expressions (e.g. ``Model.name.asc()``). Applied only when the client supplies no ``order_by``. Overrides ``deterministic_ordering``: when set, an ordering is always emitted; the primary-key tiebreaker is still appended when ``deterministic_ordering`` is True. | <code>None</code>
`distinct_on` | <code>FieldSpec \| [type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[EnumDTO] \| None</code> | The enum type for 'distinct on' clauses (PostgreSQL). | <code>None</code>
`pagination` | <code>bool \| DefaultOffsetPagination \| None</code> | Enables pagination for the field. Can be True for default offset pagination or a DefaultOffsetPagination instance for customization. | <code>None</code>
`arguments` | <code>list[StrawberryArgument] \| None</code> | A list of additional StrawberryArgument instances for the field. | <code>None</code>
`model_field` | <code>str \| None</code> | Name of the model attribute this field maps to. Lets a schema field use a different name than the underlying model field. Raises StrawchemyFieldError at decoration time if the named model field does not exist. | <code>None</code>
`id_field_name` | <code>str \| None</code> | The name of the ID field, used for certain operations. | <code>None</code>
`root_aggregations` | <code>bool</code> | If True, enables root-level aggregations for the field. | <code>False</code>
`filter_statement` | <code>FilterStatementCallable \| None</code> | A callable to generate a filter statement for the query. | <code>None</code>
`execution_options` | <code>dict[str, Any] \| None</code> | SQLAlchemy execution options for the query. | <code>None</code>
`query_hook` | <code>QueryHookCallable[Any] \| Sequence[QueryHookCallable[Any]] \| None</code> | A callable or sequence of callables to modify the SQLAlchemy query. | <code>None</code>
`repository_type` | <code>AnyRepositoryType \| None</code> | A custom strawberry class for data fetching logic. | <code>None</code>
`root_field` | <code>bool</code> | Indicates if this is a root-level field. | <code>True</code>
`**field_kwargs` | <code>Unpack[OutputFieldKwargs]</code> | ``strawberry.field`` arguments forwarded to the generated field (see ``OutputFieldKwargs``). ``name`` maps to the GraphQL field name. | <code>{}</code>

**Returns:**

Type | Description
---- | -----------
<code>Any</code> | A StrawchemyField instance, which is a specialized StrawberryField.

### `filter_field` {#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-filter_field}

```python
filter_field(*, ops: Sequence[ComparisonOperator] | None = None, arguments: Sequence[str] | None = None, apply: CustomFilterApply | None = None, join: JoinStrategy = 'exists', **field_kwargs: Unpack[StrawberryFieldKwargs]) -> Any
```

Declares a fine-grained filter field default.

The field's annotation supplies the comparison data type. With ``ops`` the field exposes
only those GraphQL operators; with ``apply`` it becomes a custom virtual scalar input;
with neither it force-includes the column's full default comparison.

**Parameters:**

Name | Type | Description | Default
---- | ---- | ----------- | -------
`ops` | <code>Sequence[ComparisonOperator] \| None</code> | GraphQL operator names to expose (restricted field). Mutually exclusive with ``apply``. | <code>None</code>
`arguments` | <code>Sequence[str] \| None</code> | Argument column names to expose on an aggregation function field. Only valid inside a class decorated with ``aggregate_filter``. Mutually exclusive with ``apply``. | <code>None</code>
`apply` | <code>CustomFilterApply \| None</code> | Custom filter callable ``(statement, value, *, dialect, model)`` returning a mutated ``Select``. | <code>None</code>
`join` | <code>JoinStrategy</code> | Fold-back strategy when ``apply`` is set (``"exists"`` or ``"in"``). | <code>'exists'</code>
`**field_kwargs` | <code>Unpack[StrawberryFieldKwargs]</code> | ``strawberry.field`` arguments applied to the generated GraphQL field (``name``, ``description``, ``metadata``, ``deprecation_reason``, ``directives``, ``graphql_type``). | <code>{}</code>

**Returns:**

Type | Description
---- | -----------
<code>Any</code> | A ``FilterFieldMarker`` consumed by the filter factory. Typed ``Any`` so it can sit as
<code>Any</code> | a default under any annotation.

**Raises:**

Type | Description
---- | -----------
<code>StrawchemyFieldError</code> | If ``ops`` and ``apply`` are both given, if ``arguments`` and ``apply`` are both given, or if ``join`` is unsupported.

### `update` {#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-update}

```python
update(input_type: type[Any], filter_input: type[BooleanFilterDTO], resolver: Any | None = None, *, validation: ValidationProtocol[T] | None = None, **field_kwargs: Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]) -> Any
```

Creates a Strawberry GraphQL mutation field for updating model instances.

This method generates a mutation field that handles updating existing
SQLAlchemy model instances based on filter criteria. It uses the provided
input type for the update data and a filter input type to specify which
records to update. It integrates with Strawchemy's strawberry system and
allows for custom validation.

**Parameters:**

Name | Type | Description | Default
---- | ---- | ----------- | -------
`input_type` | <code>[type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[Any]</code> | The Strawberry input type representing the data to update on the model instances. This should be a `MappedGraphQLDTO`. | *required*
`filter_input` | <code>[type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[BooleanFilterDTO]</code> | The Strawberry input type used to filter which model instances should be updated. This should be a `BooleanFilterDTO`. | *required*
`resolver` | <code>Any \| None</code> | An optional custom resolver function for the mutation. If not provided, Strawchemy will use a default resolver. | <code>None</code>
`validation` | <code>ValidationProtocol[T] \| None</code> | An optional validation protocol instance to validate the input data before the update operation. | <code>None</code>
`**field_kwargs` | <code>Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]</code> | Common ``strawberry.field`` / repository arguments (see ``MutationFieldKwargs``); ``graphql_type`` sets the mutation return type. | <code>{}</code>

**Returns:**

Type | Description
---- | -----------
<code>Any</code> | A `StrawchemyUpdateMutationField` instance, which is a specialized
<code>Any</code> | StrawberryField configured for update mutations.

### `update_by_ids` {#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-update_by_ids}

```python
update_by_ids(input_type: type[Any], resolver: Any | None = None, *, validation: ValidationProtocol[T] | None = None, **field_kwargs: Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]) -> Any
```

Creates a Strawberry GraphQL mutation field for updating model instances by IDs.

This method generates a mutation field that handles updating existing
SQLAlchemy model instances based on their primary key(s). The input type
should typically include the ID(s) of the record(s) to update and the
data to apply. It integrates with Strawchemy's strawberry system and
allows for custom validation.

**Parameters:**

Name | Type | Description | Default
---- | ---- | ----------- | -------
`input_type` | <code>[type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[Any]</code> | The Strawberry input type representing the data for updating model instances. This should be a `MappedGraphQLDTO`, usually generated by `pk_update_input`, which includes primary key fields. | *required*
`resolver` | <code>Any \| None</code> | An optional custom resolver function for the mutation. If not provided, Strawchemy will use a default resolver. | <code>None</code>
`validation` | <code>ValidationProtocol[T] \| None</code> | An optional validation protocol instance to validate the input data before the update operation. | <code>None</code>
`**field_kwargs` | <code>Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]</code> | Common ``strawberry.field`` / repository arguments (see ``MutationFieldKwargs``); ``graphql_type`` sets the mutation return type. | <code>{}</code>

**Returns:**

Type | Description
---- | -----------
<code>Any</code> | A `StrawchemyUpdateMutationField` instance, specialized for updates
<code>Any</code> | by ID.

### `upsert` {#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-upsert}

```python
upsert(input_type: type[Any], update_fields: type[EnumDTO], conflict_fields: type[EnumDTO], resolver: Any | None = None, *, validation: ValidationProtocol[T] | None = None, **field_kwargs: Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]) -> Any
```

Creates a Strawberry GraphQL mutation field for upserting model instances.

This method generates a mutation field that handles the "upsert"
(update or insert) of SQLAlchemy model instances. It uses the provided
input type, update fields enum, and conflict fields enum to determine
the behavior on conflict. It integrates with Strawchemy's strawberry
system and allows for custom validation.

**Parameters:**

Name | Type | Description | Default
---- | ---- | ----------- | -------
`input_type` | <code>[type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[Any]</code> | The Strawberry input type representing the data for the upsert operation. This should be a `MappedGraphQLDTO`. | *required*
`update_fields` | <code>[type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[EnumDTO]</code> | An `EnumDTO` specifying which fields to update if a conflict occurs and an update is performed. | *required*
`conflict_fields` | <code>[type](#strawchemy-mapper-Strawchemy-type)[EnumDTO]</code> | An `EnumDTO` specifying the fields to use for conflict detection (e.g., primary key or unique constraints). | *required*
`resolver` | <code>Any \| None</code> | An optional custom resolver function for the mutation. If not provided, Strawchemy will use a default resolver. | <code>None</code>
`validation` | <code>ValidationProtocol[T] \| None</code> | An optional validation protocol instance to validate the input data before the upsert operation. | <code>None</code>
`**field_kwargs` | <code>Unpack[MutationFieldKwargs]</code> | Common ``strawberry.field`` / repository arguments (see ``MutationFieldKwargs``); ``graphql_type`` sets the mutation return type. | <code>{}</code>

**Returns:**

Type | Description
---- | -----------
<code>Any</code> | A `StrawchemyUpsertMutationField` instance, which is a specialized
<code>Any</code> | StrawberryField configured for upsert mutations.

## `ModelInstance` {#strawchemy-instance-ModelInstance}

[source](https://github.com/gazorby/strawchemy/blob/v0.24.0/src/strawchemy/instance.py#L15)

```python
ModelInstance = Annotated[T, MapperModelInstance()]
```

When defined on a strawchemy type, it allows accessing the model instance in resolvers.

```python
@strawchemy.type(User)
class UserObjectType:
    instance: ModelInstance

    @strawberry.field
    def name(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.first_name} {self.last_name}"
```
